atoms.name: bit_and
atoms.rule: a ∧ b is bitwise AND on nonnegative integers.
atoms.plain: a ∧ b is bitwise AND on nonnegative integers.

atoms.name: bit_or
atoms.rule: a ∨ b is bitwise OR on nonnegative integers.
atoms.plain: a ∨ b is bitwise OR on nonnegative integers.

atoms.name: bit_xor
atoms.rule: a ⊻ b is bitwise XOR on nonnegative integers.
atoms.plain: a ⊻ b is bitwise XOR on nonnegative integers.

atoms.name: shift_left
atoms.rule: a ⇐ b shifts nonnegative a left by b bits; counts above 31 give NaN.
atoms.plain: a ⇐ b shifts nonnegative a left by b bits; counts above 31 give NaN.

atoms.name: shift_right
atoms.rule: a ⇒ b shifts nonnegative a right by b bits.
atoms.plain: a ⇒ b shifts nonnegative a right by b bits.

atoms.name: bit_count
atoms.rule: a ♯ counts the one bits of nonnegative a; negative inputs give NaN.
atoms.plain: a ♯ counts the one bits of nonnegative a; negative inputs give NaN.

domain.en: Values are nonnegative integers read as bit patterns; the lamps show the lowest eight bits.

settings.en: The preset that selects these atoms and defaults.
A recursive call unfolds at most this many times; larger counters give NaN.
The range of numbers in generated expressions and branch thresholds.

why.en: These atoms are one example. Atoms are chosen by the user: any function with a rule can be registered and the same three composition forms grow operators from it.

operators.name: ♥₁
operators.definition: ♥₁ a = { a ∧ a }
operators.plain: AND a with a bit by bit.

operators.name: ♠₂
operators.definition: a ♠₂ b = { (●₁₂ 6) △₅ (▽₁₆ a), if a >= 2 and a < 24 and b >= 26; ♥₁ 15, if a >= 24 and b < 5; a, else }
operators.plain: If 2 ≤ a < 24 and b ≥ 26, apply ●₁₂ to 6, then apply △₅ to the result and (▽₁₆ a); otherwise if a ≥ 24 and b < 5, apply ♥₁ to 15; otherwise return a.

operators.name: ●₃
operators.definition: a ●₃ b = { b, if a == 0; ♢₄₀ ((a ⇒ 1) ●₃ b), if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Start with b. Repeat once for each right shift of a until it reaches 0 (for a from 0 to 31): apply ♢₄₀ to the current value.

operators.name: ◆₄
operators.plain: Shift a left by the number of one bits in a bits.

operators.name: △₅
operators.definition: a △₅ b = { (a ⇐ b) ◆₄ }
operators.plain: Shift a left by b bits, then apply ◆₄ to the result.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ♤₆
operators.definition: ♤₆ a = { a ⇐ a }
operators.plain: Shift a left by a bits.

operators.name: ♠₇
operators.plain: Apply ♤₆ to b, then shift it right by ♤₆ a bits.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ○₈
operators.plain: Count the one bits of 12, then shift it left by a bits.

operators.name: ♠₉
operators.plain: Apply ◆₄ to a, then shift it right by b ◆₄ bits.

operators.name: ♢₁₀
operators.plain: XOR 19 with ♤₆ a bit by bit.

operators.name: ▼₁₁
operators.definition: a ▼₁₁ b = { (b ◆₄) ⇒ a }
operators.plain: Apply ◆₄ to b, then shift it right by a bits.

operators.name: ●₁₂
operators.definition: ●₁₂ a = { (a ◆₄) ∧ (a ♢₁₀) }
operators.plain: Apply ◆₄ to a, then AND it with a ♢₁₀ bit by bit.

operators.name: ◆₁₃
operators.plain: Count the one bits of a, then count its one bits.

operators.name: ♡₁₄
operators.plain: Apply ♤₆ to a, then XOR it with the number of one bits in a bit by bit.

operators.name: ●₁₅
operators.definition: a ●₁₅ = { (●₁₂ a) ⇒ (◆₁₃ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ●₁₂ to a, then shift it right by ◆₁₃ a bits.

operators.name: ▽₁₆
operators.definition: ▽₁₆ a = { 3 ▼₁₁ a }
operators.plain: Compute 3 ▼₁₁ a.

operators.name: ♤₁₇
operators.definition: a ♤₁₇ = { 6 ⇐ a }
operators.plain: Shift 6 left by a bits.

operators.name: ▲₁₈
operators.definition: a ▲₁₈ = { ♥₁ (a △₅ a) }
operators.plain: Apply △₅ to a and a, then apply ♥₁ to the result.

operators.name: ▲₁₉
operators.definition: a ▲₁₉ = { a ♤₁₇, if a < 11; ◆₁₃ a, if a >= 11 and a < 15; a △₅ a, else }
operators.plain: If a < 11, apply ♤₁₇ to a; otherwise if 11 ≤ a < 15, apply ◆₁₃ to a; otherwise compute a △₅ a.

operators.name: ☆₂₀
operators.definition: a ☆₂₀ b = { 0, if a >= 26 and b >= 18 and b < 31; ○₈ (a ▼₁₁ 18), else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 26 and b ≥ 18 and b < 31, return 0; otherwise apply ▼₁₁ to a and 18, then apply ○₈ to the result.

operators.name: ★₂₁
operators.definition: a ★₂₁ b = { a ◆₄, if a < 11 and b >= 22 and b < 24; 14 ⇐ a, if a >= 11 and b < 13; b △₅ b, else }
operators.plain: If a < 11 and b ≥ 22 and b < 24, apply ◆₄ to a; otherwise if a ≥ 11 and b < 13, shift 14 left by a bits; otherwise compute b △₅ b.

operators.name: ■₂₂
operators.definition: a ■₂₂ b = { b ▼₁₁ (●₁₂ a), if a >= 5 and a < 22 and b < 1; (♥₁ b) ∧ a, else }
operators.plain: If 5 ≤ a < 22 and b < 1, apply ▼₁₁ to b and (●₁₂ a); otherwise apply ♥₁ to b, then AND it with a bit by bit.

operators.name: ♧₂₃
operators.definition: a ♧₂₃ b = { a ♠₂ 6, if a >= 16 and b >= 31; a ☆₂₀ b, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 16 and b ≥ 31, compute a ♠₂ 6; otherwise compute a ☆₂₀ b.

operators.name: □₂₄
operators.definition: a □₂₄ b = { (b ●₁₅) ♧₂₃ (♤₆ b), if a < 1 and b >= 11; (♥₁ a) ∨ 1, else }
operators.plain: If a < 1 and b ≥ 11, apply ●₁₅ to b, then apply ♧₂₃ to the result and (♤₆ b); otherwise apply ♥₁ to a, then OR it with 1 bit by bit.

operators.name: ▼₂₅
operators.definition: ▼₂₅ a = { ♥₁ a, if a < 15; a ♠₉ a, if a >= 20 and a < 23; a ☆₂₀ a, else }
operators.plain: If a < 15, apply ♥₁ to a; otherwise if 20 ≤ a < 23, compute a ♠₉ a; otherwise compute a ☆₂₀ a.

operators.name: ●₂₆
operators.definition: a ●₂₆ b = { (a ♡₁₄) △₅ (▽₁₆ b), if a >= 4 and b >= 25; (a ▼₁₁ a) ♢₁₀, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 4 and b ≥ 25, apply ♡₁₄ to a, then apply △₅ to the result and (▽₁₆ b); otherwise apply ▼₁₁ to a and a, then apply ♢₁₀ to the result.

operators.name: ♣₂₇
operators.definition: a ♣₂₇ b = { 0 ⇒ b, if a >= 21 and b < 5; (0 ♢₁₀) ▼₁₁ (▽₁₆ b), if a < 20 and b >= 5 and b < 7; (b ♢₁₀) ⊻ (a ♢₁₀), else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 21 and b < 5, shift 0 right by b bits; otherwise if a < 20 and b ≥ 5 and b < 7, apply ♢₁₀ to 0, then apply ▼₁₁ to the result and (▽₁₆ b); otherwise apply ♢₁₀ to b, then XOR it with a ♢₁₀ bit by bit.

operators.name: ♧₂₈
operators.definition: a ♧₂₈ b = { (b ▲₁₉) △₅ (▼₂₅ b), if a >= 20 and a < 22 and b >= 7 and b < 24; (▼₂₅ b) ●₂₆ (▼₂₅ 1), if a < 20 and b >= 7 and b < 24; (b ♢₁₀) ∨ (b ♢₁₀), else }
operators.plain: Chooses between 3 cases by testing a and b; the cases combine ▲₁₉, △₅, ▼₂₅, ●₂₆, ♢₁₀ and ∨.

operators.name: ◇₂₉
operators.definition: a ◇₂₉ b = { (♥₁ b) ♧₂₃ (b ♤₁₇), if a < 30 and b >= 7 and b < 11; ○₈ (a ♠₉ a), if a >= 30 and b >= 11 and b < 14; (b ♤₁₇) ⊻ (2 ♤₁₇), else }
operators.plain: Chooses between 3 cases by testing a and b; the cases combine ○₈, ♠₉, ♤₁₇, ♥₁, ♧₂₃ and ⊻.

operators.name: ♥₃₀
operators.definition: a ♥₃₀ b = { a ♠₂ b, if a < 2 and b >= 5 and b < 18; ♤₆ a, if a >= 2 and b >= 3 and b < 5; a ▼₁₁ 10, else }
operators.plain: If a < 2 and b ≥ 5 and b < 18, compute a ♠₂ b; otherwise if a ≥ 2 and b ≥ 3 and b < 5, apply ♤₆ to a; otherwise compute a ▼₁₁ 10.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order and negation

operators.name: ♥₃₁
operators.definition: a ♥₃₁ = { (○₈ a) ☆₂₀ (a ♤₁₇) }
operators.plain: Apply ○₈ to a, then apply ☆₂₀ to the result and (a ♤₁₇).

operators.name: ■₃₂
operators.definition: a ■₃₂ b = { a ☆₂₀ b, if a >= 19 and a < 27 and b >= 4 and b < 9; a ♧₂₈ a, else }
operators.plain: If 19 ≤ a < 27 and b ≥ 4 and b < 9, compute a ☆₂₀ b; otherwise compute a ♧₂₈ a.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: □₃₃
operators.definition: □₃₃ a = { (▽₁₆ a) ∧ (a ♥₃₁) }
operators.plain: Apply ▽₁₆ to a, then AND it with a ♥₃₁ bit by bit.

operators.name: ♠₃₄
operators.definition: a ♠₃₄ b = { (◆₁₃ b) ▼₁₁ a }
operators.plain: Apply ◆₁₃ to b, then apply ▼₁₁ to the result and a.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ▼₃₅
operators.definition: a ▼₃₅ b = { b ♥₃₀ (▽₁₆ 8), if a < 19 and b >= 19 and b < 22; (▽₁₆ b) △₅ 26, if a >= 19 and a < 31 and b < 19; a ♠₃₄ (b ♡₁₄), else }
operators.plain: If a < 19 and b ≥ 19 and b < 22, apply ♥₃₀ to b and (▽₁₆ 8); otherwise if 19 ≤ a < 31 and b < 19, apply ▽₁₆ to b, then apply △₅ to the result and 26; otherwise apply ♠₃₄ to a and (b ♡₁₄).

operators.name: △₃₆
operators.definition: △₃₆ a = { ♥₁ (a ▼₃₅ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ▼₃₅ to a and a, then apply ♥₁ to the result.

operators.name: ◇₃₇
operators.definition: a ◇₃₇ = { a ♥₃₀ (a ▲₁₈), if a >= 9 and a < 17; a ▼₁₁ (a ▲₁₈), if a < 6; (16 ♤₁₇) △₅ 4, else }
operators.plain: If 9 ≤ a < 17, apply ♥₃₀ to a and (a ▲₁₈); otherwise if a < 6, apply ▼₁₁ to a and (a ▲₁₈); otherwise apply ♤₁₇ to 16, then apply △₅ to the result and 4.

operators.name: ♥₃₈
operators.definition: a ♥₃₈ b = { (●₁₂ 18) ♣₂₇ b, if a < 25 and b >= 30; (a ♤₁₇) □₂₄ (▽₁₆ 1), else }
operators.plain: If a < 25 and b ≥ 30, apply ●₁₂ to 18, then apply ♣₂₇ to the result and b; otherwise apply ♤₁₇ to a, then apply □₂₄ to the result and (▽₁₆ 1).

operators.name: ★₃₉
operators.definition: a ★₃₉ = { 8 ▼₃₅ (a ♯) }
operators.plain: Apply ▼₃₅ to 8 and (the number of one bits in a).

operators.name: ♢₄₀
operators.definition: ♢₄₀ a = { a △₅ (▽₁₆ a), if a < 2; a, else }
operators.plain: If a < 2, apply △₅ to a and (▽₁₆ a); otherwise return a.

operators.name: ♢₄₁
operators.definition: a ♢₄₁ b = { (□₃₃ b) ♠₃₄ (a ♤₁₇) }
operators.plain: Apply □₃₃ to b, then apply ♠₃₄ to the result and (a ♤₁₇).

operators.name: ◇₄₂
operators.definition: a ◇₄₂ b = { b, if a == 0; b ⊻ ((a ⇒ 1) ◇₄₂ b), if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Start with b. Repeat once for each right shift of a until it reaches 0 (for a from 0 to 31): replace the current value by b ⊻ the current value.

operators.name: △₄₃
operators.definition: a △₄₃ b = { b, if a == 0; a ∧ ((a ⇒ 1) △₄₃ b), if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Recurse on a (for a from 0 to 31): when a = 0 the result is b; otherwise let r be the result for a ⇒ 1, then replace r by a ∧ r.

operators.name: ♡₄₄
operators.definition: a ♡₄₄ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ♡₄₄ (b ⇒ 1)) ⇒ a, if b > 0 and b <= 31 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat once for each right shift of b until it reaches 0 (for b from 0 to 31): shift the current value right by a bits.

operators.name: ▲₄₅
operators.definition: ▲₄₅ a = { a, if a == 0; a ♧₂₈ (▲₄₅ (a ⇒ 1)), if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Recurse on a (for a from 0 to 31): when a = 0 the result is a; otherwise let r be the result for a ⇒ 1, then replace r by a ♧₂₈ r.

operators.name: ♠₄₆
operators.definition: a ♠₄₆ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ♠₄₆ (b ⇒ 1)) ♢₄₁ a, if b > 0 and b <= 31 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat once for each right shift of b until it reaches 0 (for b from 0 to 31): apply ♢₄₁ to the current value and a.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: △₄₇
operators.definition: a △₄₇ b = { a, if b == 0; a ♠₇ (a △₄₇ (b ⇒ 1)), if b > 0 and b <= 31 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat once for each right shift of b until it reaches 0 (for b from 0 to 31): replace the current value by a ♠₇ the current value.

operators.name: ■₄₈
operators.definition: a ■₄₈ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ■₄₈ (b ⇒ 1)) ▼₃₅ b, if b > 0 and b <= 31 }
operators.plain: Recurse on b (for b from 0 to 31): when b = 0 the result is a; otherwise let r be the result for b ⇒ 1, then apply ▼₃₅ to r and b.

operators.name: ♣₄₉
operators.definition: ♣₄₉ a = { a, if a == 0; (♣₄₉ (a ⇒ 1)) ▼₁₁ a, if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Recurse on a (for a from 0 to 31): when a = 0 the result is a; otherwise let r be the result for a ⇒ 1, then apply ▼₁₁ to r and a.

operators.name: ▽₅₀
operators.definition: a ▽₅₀ b = { 0, if a == 0; b ⊻ ((a ⇒ 1) ▽₅₀ b), if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Start with 0. Repeat once for each right shift of a until it reaches 0 (for a from 0 to 31): replace the current value by b ⊻ the current value.

operators.name: ■₅₁
operators.definition: ■₅₁ a = { (♥₁ a) ■₂₂ (▲₄₅ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ♥₁ to a, then apply ■₂₂ to the result and (▲₄₅ a).

operators.name: ♤₅₂
operators.definition: ♤₅₂ a = { (♣₄₉ a) ♠₂ (◆₁₃ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ♣₄₉ to a, then apply ♠₂ to the result and (◆₁₃ a).

operators.name: ○₅₃
operators.definition: a ○₅₃ = { (♤₅₂ a) ⇐ (a ♥₃₁) }
operators.plain: Apply ♤₅₂ to a, then shift it left by a ♥₃₁ bits.

operators.name: ●₅₄
operators.definition: a ●₅₄ = { (■₅₁ a) ♠₃₄ (a ◆₄) }
operators.plain: Apply ■₅₁ to a, then apply ♠₃₄ to the result and (a ◆₄).

operators.name: ◇₅₅
operators.definition: ◇₅₅ a = { (○₈ 3) ▼₃₅ (a ○₅₃) }
operators.plain: Apply ○₈ to 3, then apply ▼₃₅ to the result and (a ○₅₃).

operators.name: ♡₅₆
operators.definition: a ♡₅₆ b = { (♥₁ a) ☆₂₀ (b ○₅₃) }
operators.plain: Apply ♥₁ to a, then apply ☆₂₀ to the result and (b ○₅₃).

operators.name: □₅₇
operators.definition: a □₅₇ = { ♣₄₉ (a ▼₃₅ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ▼₃₅ to a and a, then apply ♣₄₉ to the result.

operators.name: ♥₅₈
operators.definition: ♥₅₈ a = { ♣₄₉ (a ♠₄₆ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ♠₄₆ to a and a, then apply ♣₄₉ to the result.

operators.name: □₅₉
operators.definition: □₅₉ a = { a ◇₄₂ a }
operators.plain: Compute a ◇₄₂ a.

operators.name: ●₆₀
operators.definition: ●₆₀ a = { (♣₄₉ a) ■₄₈ (■₅₁ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ♣₄₉ to a, then apply ■₄₈ to the result and (■₅₁ a).

operators.name: ♤₆₁
operators.definition: a ♤₆₁ = { (▽₁₆ a) ♧₂₃ (a □₅₇) }
operators.plain: Apply ▽₁₆ to a, then apply ♧₂₃ to the result and (a □₅₇).

operators.name: ◆₆₂
operators.definition: ◆₆₂ a = { a ▽₅₀ a }
operators.plain: Compute a ▽₅₀ a.

operators.name: ♢₆₃
operators.definition: ♢₆₃ a = { (♥₅₈ a) △₄₃ a }
operators.plain: Apply ♥₅₈ to a, then apply △₄₃ to the result and a.

operators.name: ▲₆₄
operators.definition: a ▲₆₄ b = { (◆₆₂ a) ●₃ b }
operators.plain: Apply ◆₆₂ to a, then apply ●₃ to the result and b.

operators.name: ◆₆₅
operators.definition: a ◆₆₅ b = { b ☆₂₀ (■₅₁ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ☆₂₀ to b and (■₅₁ a).

operators.name: ▼₆₆
operators.definition: a ▼₆₆ b = { (♤₅₂ b) ♠₄₆ (2 ◆₄), if a < 4 and b >= 5 and b < 11; (8 ♠₇ a) ♤₁₇, if a >= 4 and b >= 19 and b < 23; (b ▲₁₈) ⇒ 12, else }
operators.plain: If a < 4 and b ≥ 5 and b < 11, apply ♤₅₂ to b, then apply ♠₄₆ to the result and (2 ◆₄); otherwise if a ≥ 4 and b ≥ 19 and b < 23, apply ♠₇ to 8 and a, then apply ♤₁₇ to the result; otherwise apply ▲₁₈ to b, then shift it right by 12 bits.

operators.name: ♦₆₇
operators.definition: a ♦₆₇ = { a ●₃ a, if a >= 20; a ∧ a, if a >= 8 and a < 20; 21 ♤₁₇, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 20, compute a ●₃ a; otherwise if 8 ≤ a < 20, AND a with a bit by bit; otherwise apply ♤₁₇ to 21.

operators.name: □₆₈
operators.definition: a □₆₈ b = { a, if a < 11 and b >= 18 and b < 19; ◇₅₅ (a ◆₆₅ 17), if a >= 11 and a < 12 and b < 18; ●₁₂ (♢₄₀ b), else }
operators.plain: If a < 11 and b ≥ 18 and b < 19, return a; otherwise if 11 ≤ a < 12 and b < 18, apply ◆₆₅ to a and 17, then apply ◇₅₅ to the result; otherwise apply ♢₄₀ to b, then apply ●₁₂ to the result.

operators.name: △₆₉
operators.definition: a △₆₉ = { (2 ○₅₃) ■₃₂ (a □₅₇), if a >= 15; (▲₄₅ a) ♠₄₆ (a ▲₁₈), else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 15, apply ○₅₃ to 2, then apply ■₃₂ to the result and (a □₅₇); otherwise apply ▲₄₅ to a, then apply ♠₄₆ to the result and (a ▲₁₈).

operators.name: ♣₇₀
operators.definition: a ♣₇₀ = { (a ▲₁₉) ☆₂₀ (a ●₁₅), if a < 6; (♢₆₃ 6) ◇₂₉ 16, if a >= 28; (a ◆₄) ⊻ (10 ●₁₅), else }
operators.plain: If a < 6, apply ▲₁₉ to a, then apply ☆₂₀ to the result and (a ●₁₅); otherwise if a ≥ 28, apply ♢₆₃ to 6, then apply ◇₂₉ to the result and 16; otherwise apply ◆₄ to a, then XOR it with 10 ●₁₅ bit by bit.

operators.name: ☆₇₁
operators.definition: a ☆₇₁ b = { (◆₁₃ 0) △₄₃ (a ♤₆₁), if a < 31 and b >= 21; (■₅₁ 0) ♯, else }
operators.plain: If a < 31 and b ≥ 21, apply ◆₁₃ to 0, then apply △₄₃ to the result and (a ♤₆₁); otherwise apply ■₅₁ to 0, then count its one bits.

operators.name: ●₇₂
operators.definition: a ●₇₂ = { a ♢₄₁ 1, if a >= 7 and a < 10; ♤₅₂ a, if a >= 10 and a < 14; a □₆₈ a, else }
operators.plain: If 7 ≤ a < 10, compute a ♢₄₁ 1; otherwise if 10 ≤ a < 14, apply ♤₅₂ to a; otherwise compute a □₆₈ a.

operators.name: ▼₇₃
operators.definition: a ▼₇₃ = { (▽₁₆ a) ▲₁₈, if a < 2; (△₃₆ a) ▽₅₀ (1 ♦₆₇), else }
operators.plain: If a < 2, apply ▽₁₆ to a, then apply ▲₁₈ to the result; otherwise apply △₃₆ to a, then apply ▽₅₀ to the result and (1 ♦₆₇).

operators.name: ♢₇₄
operators.definition: ♢₇₄ a = { 6, if a >= 19 and a < 28; (♤₅₂ a) □₆₈ (a ●₇₂), if a >= 14 and a < 19; (a ♢₄₁ a) ◆₄, else }
operators.plain: If 19 ≤ a < 28, return 6; otherwise if 14 ≤ a < 19, apply ♤₅₂ to a, then apply □₆₈ to the result and (a ●₇₂); otherwise apply ♢₄₁ to a and a, then apply ◆₄ to the result.

operators.name: ♡₇₅
operators.definition: ♡₇₅ a = { a, if a < 6; (□₅₉ 21) △₆₉, if a >= 6 and a < 25; ◆₆₂ (a ⊻ 5), else }
operators.plain: If a < 6, return a; otherwise if 6 ≤ a < 25, apply □₅₉ to 21, then apply △₆₉ to the result; otherwise XOR a with 5 bit by bit, then apply ◆₆₂ to the result.

operators.name: ◆₇₆
operators.definition: a ◆₇₆ b = { b, if a == 0; ((a ⇒ 1) ◆₇₆ b) ♣₇₀, if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Start with b. Repeat once for each right shift of a until it reaches 0 (for a from 0 to 31): apply ♣₇₀ to the current value.

operators.name: ◆₇₇
operators.definition: a ◆₇₇ b = { b, if a == 0; a ▽₅₀ ((a ⇒ 1) ◆₇₇ b), if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Recurse on a (for a from 0 to 31): when a = 0 the result is b; otherwise let r be the result for a ⇒ 1, then replace r by a ▽₅₀ r.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ◆₇₈
operators.definition: a ◆₇₈ b = { b, if a == 0; ♣₄₉ ((a ⇒ 1) ◆₇₈ b), if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Start with b. Repeat once for each right shift of a until it reaches 0 (for a from 0 to 31): apply ♣₄₉ to the current value.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ▲₇₉
operators.definition: a ▲₇₉ b = { b, if a == 0; b ▽₅₀ ((a ⇒ 1) ▲₇₉ b), if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Start with b. Repeat once for each right shift of a until it reaches 0 (for a from 0 to 31): replace the current value by b ▽₅₀ the current value.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ★₈₀
operators.definition: a ★₈₀ b = { a, if b == 0; ▲₄₅ (a ★₈₀ (b ⇒ 1)), if b > 0 and b <= 31 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat once for each right shift of b until it reaches 0 (for b from 0 to 31): apply ▲₄₅ to the current value.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ☆₈₁
operators.definition: a ☆₈₁ = { a, if a == 0; a ♠₄₆ ((a ⇒ 1) ☆₈₁), if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Recurse on a (for a from 0 to 31): when a = 0 the result is a; otherwise let r be the result for a ⇒ 1, then replace r by a ♠₄₆ r.

operators.name: ♠₈₂
operators.definition: ♠₈₂ a = { a, if a == 0; (♠₈₂ (a ⇒ 1)) ◆₆₅ a, if a > 0 and a <= 31 }
operators.plain: Recurse on a (for a from 0 to 31): when a = 0 the result is a; otherwise let r be the result for a ⇒ 1, then apply ◆₆₅ to r and a.

operators.name: ■₈₃
operators.definition: ■₈₃ a = { a ◆₇₆ a }
operators.plain: Compute a ◆₇₆ a.

operators.name: ♠₈₄
operators.definition: a ♠₈₄ = { a ★₈₀ a }
operators.plain: Compute a ★₈₀ a.

operators.name: ◇₈₅
operators.definition: a ◇₈₅ b = { (■₈₃ b) ♣₂₇ (♤₅₂ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ■₈₃ to b, then apply ♣₂₇ to the result and (♤₅₂ a).

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ★₈₆
operators.definition: a ★₈₆ b = { (♢₇₄ a) ▲₇₉ (b ♠₈₄) }
operators.plain: Apply ♢₇₄ to a, then apply ▲₇₉ to the result and (b ♠₈₄).

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ♥₈₇
operators.definition: a ♥₈₇ = { (♠₈₂ a) ■₃₂ (●₆₀ 11) }
operators.plain: Apply ♠₈₂ to a, then apply ■₃₂ to the result and (●₆₀ 11).

operators.name: ♥₈₈
operators.definition: ♥₈₈ a = { (a ♠₈₄) ⊻ a }
operators.plain: Apply ♠₈₄ to a, then XOR it with a bit by bit.

operators.name: △₈₉
operators.definition: a △₈₉ = { (●₆₀ a) ★₈₀ (2 ★₃₉) }
operators.plain: Apply ●₆₀ to a, then apply ★₈₀ to the result and (2 ★₃₉).

operators.name: ●₉₀
operators.definition: a ●₉₀ = { (♥₈₈ a) △₅ (♥₈₈ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ♥₈₈ to a, then apply △₅ to the result and (itself).

operators.name: ♥₉₁
operators.definition: ♥₉₁ a = { (●₁₂ a) ◇₈₅ (♢₆₃ 0) }
operators.plain: Apply ●₁₂ to a, then apply ◇₈₅ to the result and (♢₆₃ 0).

operators.name: ♠₉₂
operators.definition: a ♠₉₂ b = { (♠₈₂ a) ▽₅₀ (b ●₅₄) }
operators.plain: Apply ♠₈₂ to a, then apply ▽₅₀ to the result and (b ●₅₄).

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ♥₉₃
operators.definition: ♥₉₃ a = { (♥₈₈ a) ▽₅₀ (3 ○₅₃) }
operators.plain: Apply ♥₈₈ to a, then apply ▽₅₀ to the result and (3 ○₅₃).

operators.name: ★₉₄
operators.definition: a ★₉₄ b = { (b ○₅₃) ◆₇₆ (a ◇₃₇), if a < 0 and b >= 14; a, else }
operators.plain: If a < 0 and b ≥ 14, apply ○₅₃ to b, then apply ◆₇₆ to the result and (a ◇₃₇); otherwise return a.

operators.name: ♡₉₅
operators.definition: ♡₉₅ a = { ■₈₃ (a ♠₈₄), if a >= 27; a ◆₇₆ (1 ♢₁₀), else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 27, apply ♠₈₄ to a, then apply ■₈₃ to the result; otherwise apply ◆₇₆ to a and (1 ♢₁₀).

operators.name: ★₉₆
operators.definition: a ★₉₆ b = { ◆₆₂ (a △₄₃ 20), if a >= 24 and a < 25 and b >= 4; (a ★₃₉) ●₃ (●₁₂ 0), if a >= 25 and b >= 4; b ◆₇₆ (♥₈₈ b), else }
operators.plain: If 24 ≤ a < 25 and b ≥ 4, apply △₄₃ to a and 20, then apply ◆₆₂ to the result; otherwise if a ≥ 25 and b ≥ 4, apply ★₃₉ to a, then apply ●₃ to the result and (●₁₂ 0); otherwise apply ◆₇₆ to b and (♥₈₈ b).

operators.name: ♥₉₇
operators.definition: a ♥₉₇ b = { b ♯, if a < 0 and b >= 5 and b < 9; 3, if a >= 0 and a < 7 and b >= 5 and b < 9; a ★₉₄ b, else }
operators.plain: If a < 0 and b ≥ 5 and b < 9, count the one bits of b; otherwise if 0 ≤ a < 7 and b ≥ 5 and b < 9, return 3; otherwise compute a ★₉₄ b.

operators.name: ☆₉₈
operators.definition: a ☆₉₈ b = { (10 ★₃₉) ♠₉₂ (◇₅₅ b), if a < 3 and b >= 3 and b < 28; 9, else }
operators.plain: If a < 3 and b ≥ 3 and b < 28, apply ★₃₉ to 10, then apply ♠₉₂ to the result and (◇₅₅ b); otherwise return 9.

operators.name: ◆₉₉
operators.definition: a ◆₉₉ b = { (6 △₄₇ b) ●₉₀, if a >= 22 and a < 29 and b < 17; ♤₆ b, if a < 22 and b < 17; (a ★₈₆ b) ♤₆₁, else }
operators.plain: If 22 ≤ a < 29 and b < 17, apply △₄₇ to 6 and b, then apply ●₉₀ to the result; otherwise if a < 22 and b < 17, apply ♤₆ to b; otherwise apply ★₈₆ to a and b, then apply ♤₆₁ to the result.

operators.name: ☆₁₀₀
operators.definition: a ☆₁₀₀ b = { a ●₃ (▽₁₆ a), if a < 1 and b >= 14 and b < 26; (♤₆ a) ◇₈₅ b, if a >= 25 and b >= 26; (b ▲₇₉ b) ♣₇₀, else }
operators.plain: If a < 1 and b ≥ 14 and b < 26, apply ●₃ to a and (▽₁₆ a); otherwise if a ≥ 25 and b ≥ 26, apply ♤₆ to a, then apply ◇₈₅ to the result and b; otherwise apply ▲₇₉ to b and b, then apply ♣₇₀ to the result.
